bounds.note: Three bounds are EXTERNAL — facts about rating systems rather than about this generator — and they are named in the findings that use them. Everything else is ordinal, distributional, or an arithmetic identity.

findings.question: TTC PD rises through the performing scale
findings.detail: no inversion beyond the sampling noise of the grades
findings.basis: Ordinal, with one tolerance rule used everywhere: a fall counts when it exceeds two standard errors of the two grades' means. TTC has no within-grade variance, so that reduces to strict monotonicity; PIT and lifetime carry a borrower-specific remainder, so a thinly populated grade may sit below its neighbour on the mix of a handful of names.

findings.question: PIT 12m PD rises through the performing scale
findings.detail: no inversion beyond the sampling noise of the grades; 1 within it: A+->A
findings.basis: Ordinal, with one tolerance rule used everywhere: a fall counts when it exceeds two standard errors of the two grades' means. TTC has no within-grade variance, so that reduces to strict monotonicity; PIT and lifetime carry a borrower-specific remainder, so a thinly populated grade may sit below its neighbour on the mix of a handful of names.

findings.question: lifetime PD rises through the performing scale
findings.detail: no inversion beyond the sampling noise of the grades
findings.basis: Ordinal, with one tolerance rule used everywhere: a fall counts when it exceeds two standard errors of the two grades' means. TTC has no within-grade variance, so that reduces to strict monotonicity; PIT and lifetime carry a borrower-specific remainder, so a thinly populated grade may sit below its neighbour on the mix of a handful of names.

findings.question: the ECL rate rises through the scale
findings.detail: Spearman 1.000 across the nineteen grades
findings.basis: Rank, not step: the provision rate is PD x LGD, and LGD is a property of the security. A grade whose names are better secured may carry a lower rate than the grade above it, which is the collateral working rather than the scale failing. A grade holding one borrower is excluded from the reversal test for the same reason the PD ordering excludes it: one name's collateral is not a statement about a scale.

findings.question: Stage 2 incidence rises with weakness
findings.detail: Spearman 0.977 between grade rank and Stage 2 share
findings.basis: Rank, not level: staging is a threshold rule, so the share steps rather than glides. Strong at >= 0.5.

findings.question: LGD does not simply track the rating
findings.detail: Spearman 0.259 between grade rank and LGD — LGD is driven by collateral, which is checked in its own section
findings.basis: Economic: loss given default is a property of the security, not of the obligor's probability of default.

findings.question: the D grade is exactly the defaulted population
findings.detail: 127 borrowers, 100% flagged, 100% in Stage 3
findings.basis: Definitional: D is assigned on the default event.

findings.question: TTC PD is a fixed property of the grade
findings.detail: constant for every grade in every quarter
findings.basis: Definitional: through-the-cycle means the grade's own level, so any portfolio movement in weighted TTC must come from migration and not from the level.

findings.question: PIT PD reacts to the cycle
findings.detail: Spearman -0.868 against the credit cycle factor (TTC -0.768); PIT/TTC ranges 0.70-1.32
findings.basis: Ordinal and signed: a point-in-time PD must fall when the economy improves. The magnitude is not asserted.

findings.question: the portfolio's weighted TTC moves only by migration
findings.detail: weighted TTC 1.47%-5.24% (3.58x) against PIT 6.43x — the grade absorbs part of the cycle by design
findings.basis: Reported, not bounded: with TTC fixed per grade the only way the weighted figure can move is the mix.

findings.question: lifetime PD is never below the 12-month PD
findings.detail: 0 violation(s) in 52,989 borrower-quarters
findings.basis: Arithmetic: a cumulative hazard over 4.2 years cannot be below the same hazard over one.

findings.question: provision intensity escalates Stage 1 < 2 < 3
findings.detail: holds in all 16 quarters
findings.basis: Ordinal, and structural: Stage 2 and 3 are measured on a lifetime PD and Stage 1 on twelve months.

findings.question: credit quality worsens Stage 1 -> 2 -> 3
findings.detail: holds in all 16 quarters
findings.basis: Ordinal.

findings.question: Stage 3 is exactly the credit-impaired population
findings.detail: 127 borrowers in Q2 2026, every one rated D, flagged and past due
findings.basis: Definitional: 90 days past due is the presumption of default and nothing in this book rebuts it.

findings.question: Stage 2 does not cure implausibly fast
findings.detail: mean 21.0% of Stage 2 exposure returns to Stage 1 each quarter (min 0.0, max 33.7); the bound is 25.0%
findings.basis: EXTERNAL: a cure rate above roughly a quarter per quarter implies an average Stage 2 sojourn under four quarters, which reads as a staging rule measuring noise rather than credit.

findings.question: Stage 3 does not cure back within a quarter
findings.detail: maximum 0.00% of Stage 3 leaves Stage 3 in one quarter
findings.basis: Methodology: this generator seasons a default for several quarters before it may cure or be written off.

findings.question: Stage 2 entry moves with the cycle without a jump
findings.detail: S1->S2 ranges 4.4%-8.2% per quarter
findings.basis: Distributional: a portfolio-wide jump with no credible event behind it is the failure mode; a range this wide is a cycle.

findings.question: the Stage 2 population never dominates the book
findings.detail: Stage 2 share ranges 11.3%-24.1% across the window
findings.basis: Distributional: a swing to portfolio dominance without a credible event is the failure this checks for.

findings.question: a rating is carried, not recomputed each quarter
findings.detail: 90.7% of borrowers hold the same grade quarter to quarter (min 87.6, max 97.9); the bound is 80.0%. Mean absolute movement 0.16 notches
findings.basis: EXTERNAL: this is a fact about rating systems rather than about this generator. A grade that changes for most of the book every quarter is a re-binned score, not a rating.

findings.question: multi-notch downgrades are uncommon
findings.detail: 0.59% fall three or more notches in a quarter (max 1.32); the bound is 3.0%
findings.basis: EXTERNAL: a three-notch fall is a credit event, not a routine quarter.

findings.question: strong grades are at least as stable as weak ones
findings.detail: Spearman -0.506 between grade rank and stability — negative or flat means strong grades are stickier
findings.basis: Ordinal: a rating system built on investment-grade names does not move them more often than it moves distressed ones.

findings.question: the ends of the scale are not one-way streets
findings.detail: stability at the extremes: AAA 83%, C 66%
findings.basis: Structural: the strongest grade has nowhere to be upgraded to and the weakest performing grade nowhere to fall short of default, so an unsmoothed assignment pushes both off their grade every quarter.

findings.question: Downside ECL >= Base ECL >= Upside ECL
findings.detail: holds in all 16 quarters, by construction from the governed weights (('Base', 0.5, 1.0), ('Upside', 0.2, 0.72), ('Downside', 0.3, 1.46))
findings.basis: Structural: the book stores ONE probability-weighted figure and the weights beside it, so the three legs are reconstructed rather than stored. The ordering is a property of the multipliers.

findings.question: the weighted figure reconciles to the scenario weights
findings.detail: maximum difference 0.000000 on a book of 1,414,950
findings.basis: Arithmetic identity.

findings.question: no impossible provision
findings.detail: no provision above its exposure, none negative, no negative overlay
findings.basis: Definitional.

findings.question: Stage 3 loss is severe rather than nominal
findings.detail: Stage 3 provision covers 56.5% of Stage 3 exposure
findings.basis: Derived from this book: a defaulted borrower carries a PD at the ceiling and an LGD around 56%, so its coverage cannot be a Stage 1 number.

findings.question: no unexplained portfolio-wide provision jump
findings.detail: largest quarter-on-quarter change in the book's ECL rate 26.7%
findings.basis: Distributional: the provision rate follows the cycle, so it moves; what it must not do is step.

findings.question: LGD falls as collateral coverage rises
findings.detail: Spearman -0.661 across 3,241 borrowers; LGD 61.5% with no collateral down to 34.7% above full coverage
findings.basis: Rank across borrowers, with band reversals judged against each band's own standard error: the bands hold between ninety and a thousand names, so a step-by-step test on the band means would be testing the bucketing rather than the economics.

findings.question: no impossible collateral position
findings.detail: recognised collateral never exceeds gross, secured never exceeds exposure, unsecured never negative
findings.basis: Definitional.

findings.question: the haircut on secured exposure is worth having
findings.detail: secured LGD 22.1% against unsecured 62.2%
findings.basis: Ordinal.

findings.question: EAD is drawn plus CCF times undrawn
findings.detail: maximum difference 0.2635 on exposures up to 8,216; 245 of 3,241 rows differ by more than a hundredth, which is the two-decimal storage
findings.basis: Arithmetic identity, to the precision the lake stores.

findings.question: CCF is reported by stage
findings.detail: CCF by stage: S1 0.356, S2 0.356, S3 0.351 — a spread of 0.005, so drawdown behaviour does not differentiate by stage in this methodology
findings.basis: Reported, not bounded: this generator does not claim that drawdown behaviour varies with deterioration, so a flat CCF is the methodology rather than a defect. It is stated because a reader comparing against a real book will expect it to vary.

findings.question: a borrower's exposure does not lurch
findings.detail: median quarter-on-quarter move: ead 5.5%, final_ecl 47.2%
findings.basis: Distributional, and reported as percentiles rather than bounded: an individual borrower may genuinely halve.

findings.question: the rating is the slowest-moving thing on the record
findings.detail: median notch movement 0, p95 1, max 15; 9.8% of borrowers change stage in a quarter
findings.basis: Ordinal: a rating is a considered assessment, so the typical borrower's grade should not move at all in a given quarter.

findings.question: every sampled borrower's trajectory reads sensibly
findings.detail: 20 borrowers over up to eight quarters, no incoherent trajectory
findings.basis: Ordinal, per borrower: a grade that moves must move with the PD, a Stage 3 quarter must carry a default trigger, and a provision must follow the risk that produced it.

findings.question: sectors differentiate risk
findings.detail: ECL rate ranges 0.09% to 15.53% — a spread of 173.1x across 17 sectors; the bound is 3.0x
findings.basis: Ordinal, and the bound differs by cut because a sector is an economic exposure. A cut that produced the same risk everywhere would not be a risk cut; holding a size cut to an economic cut's bar would demand a difference that should not exist.

findings.question: sectors do not all respond to the cycle alike
findings.detail: correlation with the credit cycle ranges -0.97 to -0.05; most cyclical Education, most resilient Government-Related Entities
findings.basis: Distributional: a book whose every sector moved together would have one risk factor, not a sector dimension.

findings.question: segments differentiate risk
findings.detail: ECL rate ranges 2.70% to 4.05% — a spread of 1.5x across 5 segments; the bound is 1.3x
findings.basis: Ordinal, and the bound differs by cut because a segment is a size and type cut, not an economic exposure, so it differentiates risk without differentiating cyclicality. A cut that produced the same risk everywhere would not be a risk cut; holding a size cut to an economic cut's bar would demand a difference that should not exist.

findings.question: segments are reported for cyclicality, not held to it
findings.detail: correlation with the credit cycle ranges -0.95 to -0.80 — every segment is cyclical, which is what this cut should show
findings.basis: Reported, not bounded: cyclicality lives in the sector dimension. A segment is a size and type cut, not an economic exposure, so it differentiates risk without differentiating cyclicality.

findings.question: the point-in-time PD worsens as the cycle turns down
findings.detail: Spearman -0.868 against the credit cycle factor
findings.basis: Signed and ordinal: the direction is the claim; the magnitude is a calibration this book does not assert.

findings.question: the Stage 2 share worsens as the cycle turns down
findings.detail: Spearman -0.950 against the credit cycle factor
findings.basis: Signed and ordinal: the direction is the claim; the magnitude is a calibration this book does not assert.

findings.question: the provision rate worsens as the cycle turns down
findings.detail: Spearman -0.924 against the credit cycle factor
findings.basis: Signed and ordinal: the direction is the claim; the magnitude is a calibration this book does not assert.

findings.question: the cycle is not counted twice
findings.detail: the point-in-time PD tracks the cycle at |0.868| and the migration-driven TTC at |0.768| — the grade absorbs part of the cycle and the conditioning adds only the remainder
findings.basis: Structural: the grade carries a documented share of the cycle, so the conditioning applies only what the grade has not.

findings.question: Stage 3 and the default population are the same names
findings.detail: 1,470 Stage 3 borrower-quarters audited across 16 quarters; every one flagged, rated D and past due, and no triggered borrower left outside Stage 3
findings.basis: Definitional, both ways: 90 days past due or a recorded default is the presumption, and nothing in this book rebuts it — so the implication runs in both directions.

findings.question: Is the performing scale the governed nineteen grades, in order, ending in C?
findings.detail: The scale is AAA AA+ AA AA- A+ A A- BBB+ BBB BBB- BB+ BB BB- B+ B B- CCC CC C.
findings.basis: The authoritative order, written out rather than counted.

findings.question: Is default a separate state rather than the scale's last grade?
findings.detail: Default is D at ordinal 20, outside the 19 performing grades.
findings.basis: A scale ending in D makes its weakest grade's default rate 100% by construction, which is unmeasurable rather than severe.

findings.question: Does every borrower carry a grade the scale defines?
findings.detail: Every rating is on the governed scale.

findings.question: Does internal_rating_ordinal agree with internal_rating on every record?
findings.detail: All 3,241 records agree.
findings.basis: They are written from the same index, so a disagreement means one of them was recomputed somewhere it should not have been.

findings.question: Does TTC PD rise as the grade weakens, across the grades the book populates?
findings.detail: Spearman rank correlation with the rating ordinal is 1.000 over 14 populated grades.
findings.basis: Rank correlation rather than strict monotonicity: two adjacent grades holding a few dozen names each can cross on their own mix, which is sampling and not a broken scale. TTC carries no such noise and is held to 0.999.

findings.question: Is C plainly the weakest PERFORMING grade and plainly not default?
findings.detail: C carries a TTC PD of 62.289%, the highest on the performing scale, against the 100% that belongs to default alone.
findings.basis: A property of the masterscale, not of this quarter's population: a quarter holding no C-rated name says nothing about where C sits on the scale.

findings.question: Is the investment-grade end low enough to be worth having?
Is every Stage 3 exposure measured at a PD of 100%?
findings.detail: 127 Stage 3 borrower(s); applicable PD ranges 100.00% to 100.00%.

findings.question: Is a Stage 3 provision its LGD rather than its exposure?
findings.detail: The largest gap between the provision and LGD x EAD is 0.0000. Coverage runs 24.0% to 92.4%, tracking LGD.
findings.basis: PD of 100% is not LGD of 100%. A defaulted borrower with collateral still recovers, and the scenario weighting does not apply to a default that has already resolved.
